local_checks.result: Profile mutations derive userId from req.ctx, whitelist writable columns, and cannot change email, password, status, organization or role through the profile body. Session listing is user-scoped; revocation first checks session ID and user ID together. Account disable affects only the current user and revokes that user's sessions. Normal registrations therefore cannot obtain an onboarding token through this path. tests/auth-plan.test.ts catches the failure and substitutes a mock token.

Onboarding completion never sets registrations.completedAt and does not compare onboardingTokenHash or onboardingExpiresAt. Do not claim a presently reachable replay or reactivation exploit: public acquisition of the required signed onboarding capability is blocked by the email/user-ID mismatch. Re-review these lifecycle checks when that functional defect is corrected.

Refresh's missing-member fallback owner claim is not a demonstrated privilege escalation: authenticate rejects absent memberships and derives the role from the current membership instead of trusting the JWT role.

Login checks pending but not disabled status, so a disabled user with the password can receive newly issued tokens and login metadata. Protected routes independently reject disabled users; no restored protected-resource access was established.

Missing owner middleware and optional confirmEmail on self-disable disagree with DESIGN.md, but the request cannot select another user or delete the organization. Treat as product-policy/self-protection issues absent additional boundary impact.

PATCH /me returns the complete updated user row, including passwordHash, to that same authenticated user. Minimize the returned projection, but no cross-principal password-hash disclosure was established.

Session listing/counting includes expired but unrevoked rows, and refresh replaces remembered-session lifetime with a fixed twelve-hour expiry. These are functional/session-UX issues, not established privilege gain.

JWT issuer/audience and explicit algorithm restrictions, strict payload schemas, constant-time OTP hash comparison and a required non-default pepper are defense-in-depth opportunities; no accepted forged credential or cross-context verifier was established.
No cookie authentication is source-established; protected mutations require explicit Bearer headers. Ordinary ambient-cookie CSRF was therefore not promoted.

local_checks.invariant: A logical sale executes once, its stock ledger remains attached to that sale, cancellation reverses its original effects once, and monetary totals satisfy the documented bounds.
local_checks.result: Creation transactions lock existing stock balances and atomically persist sale/items/stock/aggregates. Document numbering uses a transactional counter upsert. These controls do not reserve idempotency keys, serialize cancellation decisions, constrain the movement-reference rewrite to the current sale, snapshot reversal quantities, or reject excessive discounts. Existing idempotency tests mock an already-populated cache; stock tests simulate or bypass the transaction callback rather than establishing actual PostgreSQL concurrency behavior.

local_checks.invariant: Only one shift can be open per outlet, and final drawer reconciliation must correspond to the committed sale/cancellation totals.
local_checks.result: Shift opening uses a separate lookup and insert without uniqueness on open outlet shifts. Closing reads totals and status before an unconditional update; sale creation and cancellation update attached shifts without requiring open status or recomputing the reconciliation. Expense totals are server-derived, but patch derives them from an unlocked prior read. Expense creation intentionally does not receive stock. WITA day checks are present, whereas sales list date filters use UTC day endpoints rather than WITA boundaries.

unresolved: Actual PostgreSQL race schedules, rollback behavior, response persistence, and dummy-record results require a parent-approved OS-enforced sandbox; none was available.
hardening: Expense supplierId accepts a UUID without an organization-bound supplier lookup on create or patch. No supplier-name join or mutation of the referenced supplier was established in these expense paths, so this is not promoted to a demonstrated cross-tenant disclosure or write.

Expense patch calculates totalIdr using an unlocked prior row read. Concurrent authorized quantity and price patches can leave total inconsistent with the final field combination; use an atomic expression or locked read/update and add a real database concurrency regression.

Sale and expense quantities accept more than four fractional digits while storage uses numeric(14,4); calculations occur before storage rounding. Align accepted precision with persisted quantities and verify bounds and safe monetary arithmetic.

Sales date filters construct UTC calendar-day boundaries despite the WITA filtering requirement. Use the existing WITA range helper consistently; no independent privilege boundary impact was established.

Idempotency scope omits active outlet and uses originalUrl, so an outlet change can replay another outlet's response and alternate route aliases do not share a logical-operation namespace. No cross-principal disclosure is claimed because cache lookup includes organization and user.
